data.long_meaning: The name Alaudeen is derived from the Arabic language and means 'the light of the religion'. This name is a reminder of the importance of following the teachings of Islam and striving to lead a righteous and virtuous life. The name Alaudeen carries the meaning “The light of the religion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Alaudeen usually hope their child will grow to embody the light of the religion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Alaudeen Al-Mansur, the founder of Cairo in 969 AD, was the fourth Fatimid Caliph and the first to rule from Al-Qahira (Old Cairo) instead of Al-Mansuriyya (Later Mansurah) as his predecessors had done. His name Al-Mansur means 'the Victorious' or 'the Conqueror', and Al-Mansur Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah Al-Hakim appointed him as his successor while he was still alive. Alaudeen is famous for building the Al-Azhar Mosque and the Mosque of Amr Ibn El-As in Cairo.

Sultan Alaudeen Shah Al-Jamali, a Turkish Sultan who ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1206 to 1242, is known for his military prowess and his patronage of architecture and art. He expanded the territories of the Delhi Sultanate and is said to have brought about a golden age in Indian history. His name Al-Jamali means 'the Handsome, or the Beautiful', and his reign saw the construction of numerous mosques, mausoleums, and other architectural wonders.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic name 'Alaudeen' (meaning 'light of the people') is gaining popularity in various modern contexts, especially within Islamic communities and beyond. This name is frequently seen on social media platforms where users with this name connect and engage with others around the world. Additionally, Alaudeen is increasingly being given to children in international marriages between Muslims from different countries, allowing them to carry a shared cultural and religious identity. Furthermore, the globalization of education has led to an increased interest in unique and meaningful names for students, making Alaudeen a popular choice for parents seeking to provide their children with a strong cultural and spiritual foundation.
